title: Stratified shadow mirroring with per-route cost caps and isolation
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a stratified shadow/mirroring pipeline to duplicate sampled production requests to a sandboxed shadow cluster while enforcing per-route token cost caps, PII redaction, and strict isolation. Goals: 1) enable safe validation of new model variants without impacting production latencies or stateful backends; 2) provide per-route and per-customer-tier sampling policies to reduce cost and surface representative traffic; 3) attach token-level cost accounting and enforce hard caps so shadow traffic cannot exceed configured budget; 4) produce metrics and traces for offline QA and automatic gating for rollouts (metric gates for latency, token usage, and output divergence); 5) integrate auto-rollback triggers based on divergence thresholds and resource overspend. This ticket covers the core runtime plumbing, config model, monitoring, and runbook for first rollout (routes: /v1/generate, /v1/chat; tiers: free, standard, enterprise).
acceptance_criteria: Shadow duplication duplicates request payload and metadata to a configured shadow cluster without modifying live responses or adding measurable production latency (<1ms p50 increase verified)
Sampling policies support stratification by route, customer_tier, and percentage sampling; default policy: enterprise 20%, standard 5%, free 0.5%

Per-route token-cost caps enforced at request dispatch with accounting exported to billing metrics dashboard; when cap is exceeded, future shadow requests are dropped (logged) until budget window resets

Shadow requests are fully isolated: no external side-effects (no DB writes, no calls to downstream non-idempotent endpoints) and responses are stored only in encrypted audit bucket with access controls
PII redaction pipeline runs on shadow copies (configurable whitelist/blacklist) and is validated for example tokens in unit tests

Metric gating exists: divergence score (top-k logprobs + semantic similarity) and latency histograms are computed and surfaced; a gating rule can block canary promotion if divergence > configured threshold
Auto-rollback rules implemented: if divergence > X for N minutes OR shadow cost burn rate exceeds budget by Y% for 3 consecutive windows, rollback hook triggers and notifies SRE/PM
E2E tests (integration) and load tests added; PRs reviewed and merged; runbook drafted and linked
tasks: Design: finalise sampling and cost-cap config model (confluence: Stratified Shadowing design)
Runtime: add shadow dispatcher that forks requests asynchronously, with header rewriting and PII redaction hook
Config: implement per-route and per-tenant sampling policy and cost-cap in route config schema
Infra: provision isolated shadow cluster namespace and audit-storage (encrypted S3 bucket)
Telemetry: emit token-level cost metrics, divergence metrics, and shadow budget usage to Datadog dashboard
Safety: add automatic sanitizer module to drop/replace known PII; unit tests for sanitizer
Policy: implement hard stop when cost caps exceeded and add logging/alerts
Docs & Runbook: create runbook for enabling/disabling shadowing, interpreting divergence metrics, and rollback steps
QA: create test harness that replays production-captured requests into shadow cluster and compares outputs

notes: Trade-offs: we prioritise isolation and predictable cost over absolute sampling representativeness for initial rollout. Stratified sampling means lower exposure to free-tier noise but may miss rare edge-cases from low-volume customers; plan to add targeted replays for rare routes. Autoscaling interactions: shadow cluster must be scaled independently with strict budget caps to avoid cross-impact. Next steps after ship: run 2-week enterprise pilot, tune divergence thresholds, then enable 5% standard tier sampling for broader signal.
